title: Causal span anchoring and compact metric envelopes for inference KPIs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add deterministic causal anchoring between distributed traces and compact metric envelopes emitted by the inference runtime so we can reliably reconstruct tail-latency causal chains without exploding metric cardinality. This ticket implements a lightweight envelope format, exemplar mapping to OTel/Prometheus, and a trace sampler tuned for tail capture of inference requests.
background: Current Prometheus/OTel ingestion for inference KPIs captures many request-level labels (prompt_id, user_id, model_variant, trace_id) which creates high cardinality and overwhelms downstream TSDBs. Separately, traces exist but are not reliably associated with metric points (exemplars) at 99th percentile windows, making debugging tail latencies and error cascades difficult. Prior work (ENG-361421, ENG-404321) built hybrid ingestion and decoupled producers; this ticket ties them together to provide causal linkage and compact envelopes.
motivation: Improve developer productivity for incident investigations by ensuring we can go from a noisy metric spike to a deterministic trace span that explains the root cause, while keeping metric cardinality manageable and storage costs under control.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a compact metric envelope emitted by the runtime sidecar: mandatory labels limited to model_family, model_variant_safe (hashed), tenant_shard, op_name. Include a deterministic request_fingerprint (64-bit hex) derived from canonicalized routing + prompt length + quantization mode. 2) Propagate trace_id/span_id into the envelope for possible exemplar attachment, but do not use raw user identifiers as labels. 3) Implement a tail-focused trace sampler in the sidecar that: a) deterministically samples 1% globally but uses adaptive priority sampling for requests whose inferred latency is above 90th percentile (based on a moving window), capturing up to 75% of tail traces. 4) Map metric envelopes to exemplars via OTLP bridge and ensure Prometheus remote_write/PushGateway fallback preserves exemplar->trace mapping. 5) Add schema versioning and a migration path for existing dashboards. 6) Provide a small compatibility shim for Dedicated nodes that can't push exemplars due to network constraints.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy sidecar change to 10% of inference hosts in prod region us-west-2, enable compact envelope + low-rate deterministic sampling. Validate exemplars appear in Prometheus remote_write and traces link. Phase 2 (scale): increase to 50% and enable adaptive tail sampling. Phase 3: global rollout and deprecate a set of high-cardinality labels via config flags. Each phase gated by acceptance criteria and SLO checks.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end exemplar->trace linkage works for canary hosts: given a 95th+ latency metric exemplar we can lookup a corresponding trace within 30s.
Metric cardinality for model_variant label reduces by >= 80% in the canary cohort compared to baseline (measure over 24h).
Adaptive sampler captures >= 70% of true tail (95th/99th) traces in canary traffic based on offline validation harness.
No regression in host CPU or network egress > 10% for sidecar on canary nodes.
Dashboards updated: latency/error pages show exemplar links and a new 'causal chain' drilldown that opens the trace viewer filtered to the exemplar span.
Compatibility shim passes Dedicated node integration tests (simulated air-gapped environment).
